questions.q: How do you create Databricks compute that uses the ML runtime?
options: Install scikit-learn on a standard cluster by hand every time
Deploy a container from the model registry
Select the Machine learning checkbox in the create compute UI
Enable Photon in the SQL warehouse
questions.explain: Selecting the Machine learning checkbox uses Databricks Runtime ML, which comes with common ML and deep learning libraries preinstalled.

questions.q: Why does the ML runtime set the compute's access mode to Dedicated?
options: Dedicated access is needed to read Unity Catalog data on an ML runtime
It makes training run on GPUs
It disables MLflow
It is the only mode that supports Python
questions.explain: The docs state that to access Unity Catalog data on compute running Databricks Runtime ML, the access mode must be Dedicated.

questions.q: What does mlflow.sklearn.autolog() NOT record for you in the local demo?
options: The model's parameters
The trained model
Training metrics
The test-set AUC that you computed yourself
questions.explain: Autolog captures the model, parameters and training metrics, but a custom test metric such as test AUC must be logged with mlflow.log_metric.

questions.q: Why is Databricks AutoML described as glass-box?
options: It hides all code from you
It only supports one algorithm
It never trains models
It generates source notebooks you can review, reproduce and edit
questions.explain: AutoML produces notebooks with the code behind its trials so the process is transparent and editable.

questions.q: In the quickstart, what does mlflow.set_registry_uri("databricks-uc") do?
options: Starts a GPU cluster
Makes registered models go to the Unity Catalog registry instead of the workspace registry
Deletes old runs
Switches MLflow to local tracking
questions.explain: By default the client uses the workspace model registry; this setting tells it to register models in Unity Catalog, named catalog.schema.model.
